title: Verifier run on a serialized formula
statement: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables and $u$ a binary word, and suppose every variable index in every literal of $\varphi$ is less than $|u|$. For any binary words $x,p$ with $x=p\mathbin{+\!\!+}\langle \mathrm{enc}(\varphi),u\rangle$, there are a number of steps $t\le 3|\mathrm{enc}(\varphi)|+1$ and an index $i\le |x|$ such that the verifier, started in the formula-level evaluation state with $|p|$ bits consumed, work tape storing $u$, work head at $0$, and empty output, reaches a halted configuration with $i$ input bits consumed, the same work tape and head position, and output the single bit negating the DNF value of $\varphi$ under the assignment that reads the $v$th bit of $u$ and is false for indices beyond $|u|$.
hypotheses_covered: $\varphi$ is a CNF formula over natural-number variables
every literal variable index in every clause of $\varphi$ is strictly less than $|u|$
$x=p$ concatenated with the pairing of the serialization of $\varphi$ and $u$
replaced:
Let $\varphi$ be a formula whose variable indices are all below $|u|$ for a word $u$,
let $\sigma$ be its serialization, and let the input be
$x = p \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{pair}(\sigma, u)$. Started in the formula-level
evaluation state with $|p|$ bits consumed, work word $u$, and head $0$, the
non-tautology verifier halts within some $t \le 3|\sigma| + 1$ steps, with work head
$0$ and output the single bit that negates the truth value of $\varphi$ read as a DNF
under the assignment $\alpha_u$ reading variable $v$ off the $v$-th bit of $u$ (false
beyond $|u|$).
